findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refunds probably kept landing in Buckle's Aug-Oct quarter. In Q2 (May-Jul) Buckle booked a 65bp merchandise-margin benefit from refunds (about $2.1m), and that was all of its year-to-date refund (35bp of 26-week sales); Q1 said no material funds had arrived. CBP's Phase 1 refund system opened 2026-04-20 with payment 60-90 days after acceptance, which puts the bulk of payments in July-September. Peers with Aug-Oct or Jun-Aug quarters booked large refunds: TJX Q3 FY27 (to Oct 31) had a $0.05 net EPS benefit, and Levi Q3 (to Aug 30) had 370bp of gross margin. Consensus EPS of $0.88, down 9% y/y, does not visibly include a refund. A $2-4m refund is worth about $0.03-0.06 EPS, 3-7% of the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY2026 (2026-08-21) beat $0.87 vs $0.81, with the refund disclosed in the release: +2.74%. Q1 FY2026 (2026-05-29) headline beat driven by a $19.1m one-off litigation settlement while gross margin fell 50bp: -9.13%. This name has sold a one-off-driven beat when the underlying margin was weak.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a refund, consensus EPS would not sit 9% below last year on sales that are now known to be 2.6% higher, and UBS would not be citing gross margin contraction. Buckle discloses refunds only in percentage terms after the fact and has no receivable or guidance on them, so no estimate can model it. It is still a one-off with no path to guidance (the company gives none), and investors may strip it out.
findings.independence: Different sources point the same way: TJX Q3 FY27 8-K ($0.05 tariff-refund benefit, quarter to Oct 31) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm; Levi Q3 2026 8-K (370bp from refunds) https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000094845/000009484526000048/exhibit991-3q2026pressrele.htm; NRF on Phase 1 timing (2026-04-30) https://nrf.com/blog/ieepa-tariff-refunds-are-moving-forward. These are proxies: Buckle itself has not said more refunds are pending.

findings.finding: Inventory rose 13.3% y/y to $161.4m at 2026-08-01 (vs $142.5m), against Q2 sales up only 4.6%, and the markdown reserve rose to $9.2m from $8.6m at year-end. Sales then decelerated through Q3: August comps +1.6%, September +0.5%, October -0.5%, quarter +0.6%. Last year's Q3 merchandise margin already fell 10bp, and Q2 FY2026 merchandise margin was up only about 45bp excluding the refund. Carrying that inventory into a softer quarter raises markdown risk to merchandise margin, which is the line the stock sold off on in Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY2026: gross margin -50bp (merchandise -10bp, occupancy -40bp), stock -9.13% despite a headline beat. Q2 FY2026: gross margin +40bp, stock +2.74%. Gross margin is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is down 11% in 20 days, UBS expects gross margin contraction, and consensus EBIT is down 8.5%. What is not visibly priced is the inventory build specifically: no preview found mentions it. If it were priced we would expect a deeper skew than +3.2 and estimate cuts citing inventory. Some of the build may be new stores (451 vs 442) and earlier receipts ahead of tariffs, which would reduce the markdown risk.
findings.independence: Monthly comps come from separate company releases: https://www.rttnews.com/3697505/buckle-september-sales-rise-2-2.aspx and https://finviz.com/news/416668/the-buckle-inc-reports-october-2026-net-sales. The inventory and margin figures share the Q2 10-Q/release with the refund finding but rest on different lines.

findings.finding: The revenue bar is stale. The Nov 13 preview carries $326.33m consensus revenue, but the company reported Q3 net sales of $329.2m on Nov 5, about $2.9m (0.9%) above it. At roughly 30-35% incremental flow-through that is about $1m of operating income, around $0.015 EPS, against an $0.88 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales are pre-released monthly, so the print never surprises on revenue. On 2026-11-06, the day after the October sales release, the stock fell about 5.4% (search snippet, swingtradebot listing). Sales news moves the stock in the monthly releases, not on print day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sales number has been public for two weeks. What remains is the small EPS uplift if published EPS estimates were not refreshed, and the Nov 13 preview showing the old revenue figure suggests they may not have been.
findings.independence: The consensus figure comes from https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982 (2026-11-13). The bar has a single source.

findings.finding: SG&A deleverage is the other margin swing, and it sits inside consensus. Q2 SG&A rose to 30.4% of sales from 29.0% (+140bp: marketing, store labor, health insurance, supplies) on +2.1% comps, partly cushioned by 35bp of lower incentive accruals, and buying/distribution/occupancy deleveraged 70bp. Q3 comps were only +0.6%, so deleverage likely persists or widens. A simple model (gross margin -50 to -80bp, SG&A +120 to +140bp) gives operating margin of about 17.2-17.5%, around $57m, against $56.05m consensus EBIT. That is roughly in line, with a slight downside tail if deleverage exceeds Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY2026 operating margin fell 100bp to 17.4%, yet the stock rose 2.74% on the EPS beat. Q1 FY2026's underlying SG&A rose 145bp excluding the settlement, and the stock fell 9.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus EBIT already implies about 190bp less operating margin. It is filed because the size of the deleverage on a +0.6% comp is the second unknown of the print. A worse number would only surprise if SG&A growth stepped above Q2's 9.6%.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 10-Q with findings 1 and 2, on a different line. The consensus EBIT comes from https://www.itiger.com/news/1134066982.
